3090123.findings: Carved fruitwood putto in a flying pose holding a wooden ring; better carving than the bare title suggests (smiling expressive face, crisp curled hair, good hands and feet). No signature, maker's mark, label or inscription on any of the 3 photos. Glossy shellac or varnish finish. A round wooden plug fills an old fixing hole in the back, with two small dark pin holes beside it, so it was probably once mounted on something (wall, bed canopy or furniture). The ring is a separate turned ring with bound leather or rawhide patches at the joins, which looks like an old repair. Baroque-style Continental carving (Italian or Alpine type); age cannot be proven from the photos.
3090123.condition: Sold as is. Hairline crack along the shoulder and upper arm joint of the free arm (photos 2 and 3), the arm may be a glued separate piece; round plug repair and two pin holes in the back; ring has bound repairs; glossy finish scuffed and uneven in places. Figure otherwise complete, hands and feet intact.
3090123.reason: Well carved fruitwood putto sold as is; good face and hair, possibly older Continental; crack and repairs limit value.
3090123.marks_read: none: no signature, stamp or maker's mark; only a round wood plug in the back

3090124.findings: Modern waxed pine chest, two short over three long drawers, bevelled panel-style drawer fronts, dark turned wooden knobs, scalloped apron on a plinth base. Looks like a late 20th century reproduction, not antique. No labels, stamps or maker's marks visible (single front view only; interiors, back and underside not shown).
3090124.condition: Looks sound in the one photo; light surface marks and a few knots; runners and back not visible.
3090124.reason: Modern reproduction pine chest, bulky, low resale value.

3090125.findings: Pair of brass candlesticks with bamboo-turned stems, flat drip pans and wide beaded round feet. Both undersides carry lettering around the rim: the right-hand base is stamped or engraved with partly legible words (roughly 'NOT EARN...' and '...DOUBLE...') and the left-hand base has dotted or pin-punched lettering that is illegible at this photo size (enlarged and unwrapped, still unreadable). No maker's name, registration mark or hallmark found. Recessed brown underside with a central fixing screw and a small second pin. Late Victorian to Edwardian look, but could be a later reproduction.
3090125.condition: Bright polish with light scratches and tarnish; green verdigris patches on the top of the right-hand foot; rim lettering worn; no splits, repairs or missing nozzles seen.
3090125.reason: Ordinary pair of brass candlesticks; rim lettering unexplained and mostly illegible, no maker's mark, so value stays modest.
3090125.marks_read: Underside rim lettering only partly legible (right base 'NOT EARN...' and '...DOUBLE...'); left base illegible; no maker's mark or hallmark

3090126.findings: Large oval fish platter in heavy cast aluminium with a moulded raised rim and a plain, unpatterned well; grey surface with scratches and dark oxidation spots and a pale rectangular patch (old label or tape residue) in the well. No maker's name, stamp or hallmark visible; underside not photographed. Looks like a hotel or restaurant style serving piece. Matches the title.
3090126.condition: Worn and scratched with oxidation spots; looks flat and uncracked in the one photo.
3090126.reason: Plain cast aluminium platter, unmarked, low value.

3090127.findings: Complete-looking upright (Saxony style) timber spinning wheel with a long treadle board, flyer assembly and several bobbins fitted, some with yarn. The layout resembles the Ashford Traditional pattern from New Zealand, but no maker's transfer, plate or burn mark is visible in either photo, so the maker is unproven. Accessories on the floor: a pair of wooden hand carders (blue card cloth visible), a boxed 'WOOL WINDER' (white box, red lettering, no maker's name legible), spare bobbins, a wooden-backed wool comb with steel tines, a plastic reel with a red 'Luc...' label (probably an unrelated wire reel) and a small amber bottle with a green and white label (probably wheel oil, text not legible). Not a spirits lot.
3090127.condition: Wheel looks solid and complete with drive band and bobbins; normal wear and darkening. Cannot tell if it runs freely or if the flyer hooks and orifice are intact. Accessories are used and the box shows age marks.
3090127.reason: Complete working-style timber spinning wheel with carders, bobbins and winder; maker not shown but hobby demand makes it plausibly worth real money.
3090127.marks_read: 'WOOL WINDER' box lettering and red 'Luc...' reel label only; no maker's mark on the wheel

3090128.findings: Cast brass fire companion set on a round stand with a cast foliate base: stag-head finial on the centre post and a stag head on each handle (shovel, brush with black bristles, poker and tongs appear present). Dark antique-style patina with polished highlights, typical of an imported 20th century reproduction. No maker's mark, stamp or registration number visible; underside of the base not shown.
3090128.condition: Looks complete (stand plus four tools); light tarnish, shovel blade scratched and dull.
3090128.reason: Modern cast brass stag-head companion set, unmarked, modest value.

3090129.findings: Tall trumpet vase on a round foot with a rope-twist band, plated (nickel or silver plate over brass) with the plating worn through to yellow brass in places and heavily tarnished and stained. Small white flake or chip on the upper body and grey corrosion crust inside the neck. No hallmark, EPNS mark or maker's stamp visible in the 3 photos (underside not shown); only the Armitage tag 112 on the stem.
3090129.condition: Poor: worn and stained plating with brass showing through, pitting, and corrosion inside the mouth; no obvious splits.
3090129.reason: Worn, tarnished plated trumpet vase with plating loss, no marks.

3090130.findings: Long brass club-style fire fender: round front rail on ball finials above reeded base rails, with cast leaf-pattern feet at the corners; consistent with a late Victorian date. Tarnished with verdigris on the rails and corners. No maker's name, registration diamond or stamp visible in either photo (inside face and underside not shown).
3090130.condition: Dull and tarnished with verdigris spots; no obvious breaks or missing finials in the photos; needs a clean.
3090130.reason: Ordinary late Victorian brass fender, unmarked, tarnished and bulky.

3090131.findings: Two old iron fire irons tied with black ribbon: a coal shovel with a pierced oval wreath-like emblem in the blade (not a legible crest) and a twist-stem handle with an acorn-type finial, and a plain poker with a ball knob. Dark, pitted and rusty throughout. No maker's mark, registration mark or stamp visible on either photo.
3090131.condition: Rusty and pitted; shovel blade riveted to the handle with two rivets; no breaks seen.
3090131.reason: Common old iron shovel and poker, rusty and unmarked.

3090132.findings: Slope-lid softwood storage bin with dovetailed corners (photo 2), a plain hinged lid and a vertical divider making two compartments inside (photo 3). Old pale stain or varnish with age marks. The small stock sticker on the lid has an illegible handwritten number, not a maker's mark. No branding, maker's stamp or label found inside or out.
3090132.condition: Used and scuffed, sound structure, simple iron hinges; no splits or missing parts seen.
3090132.reason: Plain utility pine storage bin, no maker or age marks, low value.

3090133.findings: Oval painted tin hat box with a faux wood-grain finish on the sides, dark top, blue painted interior, iron carrying handle on the lid and a front catch. The apparent plate on the lid is a blank grey patch (paper or metal) with no legible writing. No maker's name, label or stamp found in the 3 photos. Victorian to early 20th century style.
3090133.condition: Worn paint with rust at the lid edge and handle, flaking and scuffs on the body; interior paint mostly good with small marks; catch and hinge present.
3090133.reason: Common painted tin hat box with rust and wear, no maker's name.

3090134.findings: Two short over three long drawer pine chest on a plinth, moulded top and panelled sides, later cream paint over everything, pressed brass drop handles with rosette plates. Consistent with the Edwardian description, though the paint hides the timber and any stamp. No labels or marks visible in either photo; drawer interiors not shown.
3090134.condition: Paint chipped and worn on the edges, top and lower drawers, with scuffs and small marks; looks solid; handles complete.
3090134.reason: Ordinary painted pine chest of drawers, accurately described, bulky.

3090135.findings: Green, yellow and brown drip-glazed earthenware jardiniere with a white glazed interior, scalloped pie crust rim, rouletted rope band and incised lines at the shoulder, thrown foot. Base (photo 4) is unglazed buff clay with throwing rings and a fine crack line, with no impressed, incised or painted maker's mark. The only writing is a handwritten blue ink stock sticker 'S318/1' on the body (photo 2). Looks late 19th or early 20th century English or Australian; no maker can be shown from the photos.
3090135.condition: Damaged as catalogued: chips and loss to the scalloped rim with exposed body (photos 2 and 3), hairline or star crack in the interior floor (photo 5), a fine crack line across the base (photo 4), and glaze chips at the foot rim.
3090135.reason: Unmarked drip glaze jardiniere with chipped rim and cracks, low value.
3090135.marks_read: 'S318/1' handwritten stock sticker only; no maker's mark on the base

3090136.findings: Colour print (looks like a chromolithograph or similar reproduction, not an original painting) of Christ appearing to Mary Magdalene in the garden (Noli me tangere), in a worn gilt composition frame with a stepped moulding. No signature, publisher's name, plate mark or caption visible in the picture area; the lower margin is hidden by the frame slip. A small stock sticker at the lower right has an illegible handwritten number.
3090136.condition: Frame has worn gilt, small knocks and a tiny loss at one lower corner; print looks toned and slightly mottled with some glare, possibly glazed; frame back and print margins not seen.
3090136.reason: Common religious colour print in a worn gilt frame, no signature.

3090137.findings: Cobalt blue baluster floor vase with a flared neck and everted rim, covered in a dense pattern of cream stippled cranes and clouds with brown-gilt highlights, gilt bands at the rim and foot and a red-brown unglazed foot ring. The decoration looks printed or stencilled, typical of modern Chinese-style decorative export vases rather than antique hand painted Satsuma or Kutani. Only one photo: no marks seen and the base and interior are not shown.
3090137.condition: No cracks, chips or restoration visible in the one photo; gilt looks intact; base and inside not shown.
3090137.reason: Modern decorative Chinese-style blue and gilt floor vase, unmarked in the photo.
